instructions:
You were seen today for symptoms consistent with acute vaginitis. Vaginitis can have several causes, including bacterial vaginosis (BV), yeast infection, trichomoniasis, or sexually transmitted infections such as chlamydia or gonorrhea.

Testing Performed

We collected samples today to test for:

Bacterial vaginosis (BV)
Trichomonas
Chlamydia
Gonorrhea

Your results are currently pending. We will contact you when the results are available and discuss whether treatment is needed.

What Happens If a Test Is Positive?

Treatment will depend on your results:

Bacterial vaginosis (BV): Usually treated with an antibiotic such as metronidazole, either by mouth or as a vaginal medication.
Trichomonas: Usually treated with oral metronidazole. Because trichomonas is sexually transmitted, sexual partner(s) will also need treatment to help prevent reinfection.
Chlamydia: Usually treated with an antibiotic such as doxycycline. Recent sexual partner(s) should also be evaluated and treated.
Gonorrhea: Usually treated with an antibiotic injection (ceftriaxone). Recent sexual partner(s) should also be evaluated and treated.
If all testing is negative but your symptoms continue, you may need additional evaluation for other causes of vaginal irritation or discharge, including a possible yeast infection.
Until Your Results Return

Avoid sexual activity until your results are known. If an STI is identified, you should avoid sexual activity until you and your partner(s) have completed the recommended treatment and the appropriate waiting period has passed.

Avoid douching, scented vaginal products, and other products that may cause additional irritation.

Seek Prompt Medical Care If

Please seek immediate or prompt medical evaluation if you develop severe or worsening pelvic/lower abdominal pain, high fever, persistent vomiting, heavy or unusual vaginal bleeding, fainting/dizziness, or rapidly worsening symptoms.

If your symptoms do not improve after treatment or continue despite negative testing, follow up with your primary care clinician or OB/GYN for further evaluation.
